Draw new random effects from an estimated GAM

Source: R/random-effect-samples.R
random_effect_samples.Rd

Sample zero-mean Gaussian random effects using the fitted smoothing parameters and dispersion. These are new effects, rather than posterior draws of the effects estimated for the fitting groups.

Usage

random_effect_samples(model, data = NULL, select = NULL, n_draws, seed = NULL)

Arguments

model

An ordinary mgcv::gam() or mgcv::bam() fit with one linear predictor.

data

Evaluation data. With NULL, use the fitting observations. Supplied data need only contain predictors of the selected smooths. Group labels may be new; repeated labels share an effect within a draw.

select

Exact smooth labels, or NULL for all re and fs terms.

n_draws

Positive integer giving the number of draws.

seed

Optional integer seed. An explicit seed preserves the caller's random-number state; NULL advances the current state.

Value

A tibble of class random_effect_samples, with .row, .draw, .smooth, .value (the link-scale contribution), and covariates. The random_effect_info attribute describes the fixed covariance estimates.

Details

Standard re random intercepts, slopes and factor interactions, and fs random curves are supported. Each curve is drawn jointly over its evaluation points, including the components penalising its constant and linear parts. Custom re penalties supplied through xt$S are unsupported. Fits using min.sp are also unsupported: mgcv does not retain the fitted lower bounds needed to reconstruct their random-effect covariance.

For stored penalties \(S_j\), smoothing parameters \(\lambda_j\), and dispersion \(\phi\), coefficient covariance is $$\phi(\sum_j\lambda_j S_j)^{-1}.$$ Smoothing parameters and dispersion remain fixed. As in mgcv::gam.vcomp(), random-effect covariance uses reml.scale when it is finite and sig2 otherwise. Response generators retain their usual sig2 dispersion. Different smooths and different groups have independent new coefficients, as specified by these model terms. Covariance between fitted coefficients is not used here.

Use marginalise in fitted_values() or fitted_samples() to integrate response means over these distributions. Use it in predicted_samples(), posterior_samples() or simulate.gam() to simulate new-group responses.

Examples

load_mgcv()
m <- gam(travel ~ s(Rail, bs = "re"), data = nlme::Rail,
  method = "REML")
random_effect_samples(m, n_draws = 3, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 54 x 6
#>     .row .draw .smooth .value travel Rail 
#>    <int> <int> <chr>    <dbl>  <dbl> <ord>
#>  1     1     1 s(Rail)  34.0      55 1    
#>  2     2     1 s(Rail)  34.0      53 1    
#>  3     3     1 s(Rail)  34.0      54 1    
#>  4     4     1 s(Rail)  15.7      26 2    
#>  5     5     1 s(Rail)  15.7      37 2    
#>  6     6     1 s(Rail)  15.7      32 2    
#>  7     7     1 s(Rail)  37.5      78 3    
#>  8     8     1 s(Rail)  37.5      91 3    
#>  9     9     1 s(Rail)  37.5      85 3    
#> 10    10     1 s(Rail)  -1.56     92 4    
#> # i 44 more rows

# Compare zero random effects with response means averaged over groups.
set.seed(2)
d <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 15), id = factor(1:12))
d$y <- rpois(nrow(d), exp(0.3 + d$x + rnorm(12, sd = 0.6)[d$id]))
p <- gam(y ~ x + s(id, bs = "re"), data = d, family = poisson(),
  method = "REML")
nd <- data.frame(x = c(0, 0.5, 1), id = d$id[1])
fitted_values(p, data = nd, exclude = "s(id)")
#> # A tibble: 3 x 8
#>    .row     x id    .parameter .fitted   .se .lower_ci .upper_ci
#>   <int> <dbl> <fct> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1     1   0   1     mean          1.73 0.209      1.15      2.61
#> 2     2   0.5 1     mean          2.61 0.194      1.79      3.82
#> 3     3   1   1     mean          3.93 0.202      2.64      5.84
fitted_values(p, data = nd, marginalise = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 8
#>       x id     .row .parameter .fitted   .se .lower_ci .upper_ci
#>   <dbl> <fct> <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1   0   1         1 mean          2.14 0.447      1.26      3.02
#> 2   0.5 1         2 mean          3.22 0.624      2.00      4.44
#> 3   1   1         3 mean          4.85 0.979      2.93      6.77
fitted_values(p, data = nd, marginalise = TRUE,
  integration = "monte_carlo", seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 3 x 8
#>       x id     .row .parameter .fitted   .se .lower_ci .upper_ci
#>   <dbl> <fct> <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1   0   1         1 mean          2.12 0.444      1.25      2.99
#> 2   0.5 1         2 mean          3.20 0.619      1.98      4.41
#> 3   1   1         3 mean          4.81 0.971      2.91      6.71
nd$id <- c("new", "new", "other")
predicted_samples(p, data = nd, marginalise = TRUE, n_draws = 3, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 9 x 3
#>    .row .draw .response
#>   <int> <int>     <dbl>
#> 1     1     1         5
#> 2     2     1         6
#> 3     3     1         4
#> 4     1     2         1
#> 5     2     2         3
#> 6     3     2         4
#> 7     1     3         1
#> 8     2     3         3
#> 9     3     3        19
